# Recipe reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs`. Do not edit: run the target instead. -->

A recipe is a directory holding `recipe.yaml`, `compose.yaml`, and optionally a
`test/` directory of assets. This page is the field reference, generated from
[`schema/recipe.schema.json`](../schema/recipe.schema.json) so that it cannot
disagree with what the validator enforces.

For how to write one, start with
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#add-a-recipe-in-10-minutes) and
[`recipes/TEMPLATE`](../recipes/TEMPLATE). For why the format is shaped this way,
see [SPEC.md](../SPEC.md) section 3.

Two things the tables cannot tell you:

- **The schema validates the file as written, with `{{ ... }}` templates
  unexpanded.** That is what lets an editor and the independent validator job use
  it. Values are rendered against a restricted context - `.vars`, `.inputs` and
  `.runID`, and nothing else - after validation.
- **`compose.yaml` has its own schema**,
  [`schema/compose-safety.schema.json`](../schema/compose-safety.schema.json),
  which encodes the isolation rules. Those are hard failures, never warnings.

## The recipe document

| field | type | required | constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | const | yes | must be `restored/v1` |
| `checks` | array of `check` | yes | at least 1 items |
| `inputs` | object | yes | at least 1 keys; keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` |
| `kind` | const | yes | must be `Recipe` |
| `metadata` | object | yes |  |
| `ready` | array of `probe` |  |  |
| `test` | object |  |  |
| `vars` | object |  | keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` |

## metadata

The recipe's identity. It is prose, and it is never templated.

| field | type | required | constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string | yes | at least 20 characters |
| `maintainers` | array of string |  |  |
| `name` | string | yes | matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,38}[a-z0-9]$` |
| `tags` | array of string |  | unique items |
| `title` | string | yes | at least 3 characters; at most 80 characters |
| `upstream` | string |  | format `uri` |

## checks[]

One assertion about the restored application. Checks run once, in order, and every check runs even after an earlier one has failed.

| field | type | required | constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expect` | object | yes | at least 1 keys |
| `id` | string | yes | matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,48}$` |
| `kind` | enum | yes | one of `http`, `exec`, `sql`, `file` |
| `timeout` | `duration` |  |  |
| `title` | string | yes | at least 5 characters |

### kind: `http`

Also required: `url`.

| field | type | required | constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `basic_auth` | array of string |  | at least 2 items; at most 2 items |
| `json_body` | string |  |  |
| `method` | enum |  | one of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST` |
| `url` | `internalURL` | yes |  |

| `driver` | enum | yes | one of `postgres`, `sqlite` |
| `file` | string |  |  |
| `query` | string | yes | at least 5 characters |
| `service` | `serviceName` |  |  |
| `user` | string |  |  |

## checks[].expect

The closed vocabulary a check may assert with. A recipe is data, not a program:
there is no expression language here on purpose, and the list is kept short enough
that a reviewer can hold it in their head.

Every key present is evaluated, so a failing check reports every way it missed
rather than only the first. One trap worth naming: **`not_empty` counts directory
entries**, so it is only ever met by a directory. For a file, use `size_min: 1`.


| field | type | required | constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `body_matches` | `regex` |  |  |
| `body_not_matches` | `regex` |  |  |
| `exists` | boolean |  |  |
| `exit_code` | integer |  |  |
| `glob` | string |  |  |
| `glob_min_count` | integer |  | minimum 1 |
| `is_dir` | boolean |  |  |
| `json_path` | string |  |  |
| `json_path_equals` | string |  |  |
| `json_path_int_min` | integer |  |  |
| `json_path_len_min` | integer |  | minimum 0 |
| `not_empty` | boolean |  |  |
| `rows_max` | integer |  | minimum 0 |
| `rows_min` | integer |  | minimum 0 |
| `scalar_equals` | string |  |  |
| `scalar_int_max` | integer |  |  |
| `scalar_int_min` | integer |  |  |
| `size_min` | integer |  | minimum 0 |
| `status` | integer |  | minimum 100; maximum 599 |
| `status_in` | array of integer |  |  |
| `stderr_matches` | `regex` |  |  |
| `stdout_matches` | `regex` |  |  |

Keys that need another key present:

- `glob_min_count` needs `glob`
- `json_path_equals` needs `json_path`
- `json_path_int_min` needs `json_path`
- `json_path_len_min` needs `json_path`

## Named types

| type | definition |
|---|---|
| `absolutePath` | matches `^/(?:[^/\x00]+/)*[^/\x00]*$` |
| `duration` | matches `^[0-9]+(ns|us|ms|s|m|h)$` |
| `internalURL` | matches `^https?://[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*(:([0-9]{1,5}|\{\{[^{}]*\}\}))?(/([^\s{}]|\{\{[^{}]*\}\})*)?$` |
| `regex` | at most 512 characters |
| `serviceName` | matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` |
